subject: Invoice on hold — unlinked request IDs in usage export
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya@orionhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, accounts-payable@orionhealth.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Invoice on hold — unlinked request IDs in usage export

Hi Sean / Monica,

Our AP team put January's invoice on hold after we received the usage export you sent — there are ~18k lines that don't map to any of our tenant IDs (column: request_id). The accounting system flags these as "unlinked request" and prevents payment until we reconcile.

We dug through the CSV and found many short request IDs (8–12 chars) that look like transient proxy IDs rather than the client_request_id we normally see. Example rows attached (embed_usage_snapshot.csv). We suspect these map to your internal routing or a cache layer but we need Redwood to confirm mapping before we release payment.

Can you: 1) confirm whether those request IDs are client traffic for Orion Health; 2) provide a mapping or trace evidence we can share with our finance team; and 3) advise how Redwood will prevent this at month-end going forward?

We're currently holding $48,250 pending reconciliation. Please let us know what you need from our side (sample IDs, time windows, or a signed credit).

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Head of Finance Operations
Orion Health

Attachment: embed_usage_snapshot.csv (csv, 120 KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice on hold — unlinked request IDs in usage export

Hi Priya — thanks for flagging this and for the CSV.

Short answer: we believe these are "ephemeral request IDs" created by a transient KV-cache fallback we run when clients exceed prefix length or when a proxy strips the client_request_id header. That produces a short internal request_id that isn't immediately attributed to the customer in the export.

I'm looping Connor (infra) to pull traces for the sample IDs you sent. Connor — can you pull the traces for the first 10 request IDs in the attached CSV and confirm whether the requests originated from Orion's API keys or a misrouted proxy? If this is on us, we'll propose a credit to clear the hold and a mitigation timeline.

Priya — can you confirm the top 3 request IDs you care about and grant permission for us to share full traces with your AP team if needed? If you'd rather, we can redact payloads and only provide routing/attribution evidence.

Proposed short-term remediation: if we verify these map to Orion, Redwood will issue a one-time invoice credit equal to the unbilled amount for those events and update the usage export to include a retrospective mapping column for your ledger. We'll confirm numbers once Connor finishes the trace.

I'll follow up by EOD with a concrete plan. Apologies for the interruption to your payment flow.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@orionhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2027 15:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice on hold — unlinked request IDs in usage export

Hi all — I pulled traces for the sample set Sean asked for. Summary: 8 of the 10 request IDs map to requests that passed through our prefix-normalizer when the client_request_id header was >64 bytes and our proxy generated a short internal request_id for routing. Those short IDs are treated as first-class request identifiers in the raw logs but our post-process attribution pipeline only joins on client_request_id and api_key when available — the join missed these because the normalized proxy id wasn't copied into the attribution table.

What happened (root cause):
- Orion's integration recently started sending a very long client_request_id on a subset of calls (we see a spike starting 2026-12-27).
- Our prefix-normalizer truncated those and emitted a short proxy request_id for internal routing.
- Attribution ETL relied on the original client_request_id column; we didn't persist the proxy id into the join keys for those rows.

Impact: approximately 0.35% of January's token volume for Orion (rough estimate based on sample) — matches the ~$48k hold when we scale to total usage.

Attached: redwood_trace_20270109.txt (sanitized traces) — shows mapping for the sample IDs and the client IPs that tie the requests to Orion's network blocks.

Short-term actions (24–72 hrs):
1) We will backfill the attribution join for the affected window using the proxy request_id -> client IP heuristic (low risk, read-only to ledger).
2) Produce an export column (proxy_linked_request_id) in the usage CSV so your AP system can reconcile automatically.
3) Provide a provisional invoice credit equal to the disputed amount while we run the backfill; final credit will be reconciled after backfill validation.

Longer term: update the proxy to preserve client_request_id in the attribution keys and add an alert when request_id normalization occurs.

Let me know if you want the backfill run before or after your AP unfreezes the payment. If you want us to start immediately, we can target a completion window of 36 hours.

—Connor Obrien
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_trace_20270109.txt (sanitized text, 75 KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, accounts-payable@orionhealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice on hold — unlinked request IDs in usage export

Thanks Priya — and thank you Connor for the quick analysis.

Priya / Orion AP team — based on Connor's traces we can confirm the unlinked request IDs belong to Orion traffic. Redwood will: 1) run the attribution backfill now (target completion within 36 hours), 2) deliver an updated usage CSV with proxy_linked_request_id and rollback notes to your AP inbox, and 3) issue a provisional credit equal to the hold ($48,250) as a contra line on the January invoice. The provisional credit will remain until our backfill validation completes (expected within 5 business days).

Next steps for Orion: please reply to this email giving us permission to share the sanitized traces with your AP/finance staff and to apply the backfill while the invoice is in hold. If you'd prefer a signed mutual action (DocuSign) before we apply the credit, we can generate that — I'll attach the credit note (credit_note_ORD-693.pdf) and a DocuSign link once you confirm.

If we don't hear back by EOD tomorrow we'll apply the backfill and provisional credit to unblock payment (we'll still share the results and retain the final reconciliation window).

Appreciate your patience — we'll follow up with the updated export and credit reference once the backfill completes.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
